quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. When you see a stop sign, come to a complete stop at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Motorcyclists have the right to use the full width of a traffic lane. You should pass a motorcycle the same way you would pass any other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists need the full lane to stay safe and move around safely. Do not share a lane with motorcyclists, even if there seems to be enough room.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what should you do?

options.text: You are approaching a railroad crossing. Prepare to stop.
You will always stop at the upcoming railroad crossing.
Stop and wait for a signal before crossing the railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are approaching a railroad crossing. Prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a railroad crossing is ahead. Look and listen carefully. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you cross.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when can you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your original lane when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This means you are far enough ahead to do so safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road ahead has many curves. Slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around if you are driving toward this sign.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange signs mean work zone activity ahead. Stay alert for unexpected road conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Obey the flagger's directions.

questions.question: Can you turn right on a red light after stopping and checking for traffic and pedestrians?
questions.explanation: You may turn right at a red light unless a sign says you cannot. You must come to a complete stop first. Yield to all other drivers and pedestrians before turning.

questions.question: What can you do at a single broken white line on a highway?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to enter. It is posted on one-way streets and roads where entry is not allowed. You may see it if you try to enter an expressway ramp from the wrong direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are approaching.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers that bicycles may be crossing ahead.

questions.question: How many feet away must a driver dim their high beams before meeting another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Dim your high beams 500 feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle. Dim them 300 feet before when approaching a vehicle from behind.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks, unless a traffic signal tells them to wait.

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be ready for children on bikes to suddenly enter the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: This sign warns of a railroad crossing with no signal. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At this sign, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be ready to stop if you see or hear a train. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: What does a red octagon-shaped sign say?
questions.explanation: An octagon (eight-sided) sign always means stop. You must always come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and turn safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars disappear in blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear orange, yellow, or bright jackets and use paddles and flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: After a police officer pulls you over, should you immediately exit your vehicle and walk toward the officer's car?
questions.explanation: Stay in your vehicle with both hands visible on the steering wheel when stopped by police.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve.
Drive no slower than 35 mph through the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to conditions ahead. Speed advisory signs tell you the safe speed for the upcoming curve or condition.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction.

questions.question: Which of the following causes many traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Always drive at safe speeds within the legal limit.

questions.question: How far before turning should you signal in a business or residential area?
questions.explanation: Signal for at least 100 feet before turning in business or residential areas. In other areas, signal at least 200 feet before turning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Right turn on red light allowed with caution.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal line over a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign prohibits right turns.

questions.question: Slow vehicles should use the left lane, except when passing or making a left turn.
questions.explanation: Slow vehicles must use the right lane, except when passing or making a left turn.

questions.question: When weather or light conditions require headlights while driving, which should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive more slowly at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left. Parked vehicles are to your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Down the middle between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between both sides.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle. This keeps you away from danger on both sides.

questions.question: A train has passed at a railroad crossing. What should you do before driving?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not drive until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can use this lane in either direction.
You are near a divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic flows in both directions.

questions.question: On a two-lane road, must you stop when you approach a stopped school bus with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended?
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus loading or unloading passengers, unless it is on the opposite side of a four-lane road. Stop and wait until the stop arm goes up and the lights stop flashing, or the driver signals you to go.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicles.
questions.explanation: Follow a motorcycle with at least three to four seconds of distance. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely is dangerous for you and the rider. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid them. Falls are more likely on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.
